Manually constructed alpha signals tend to exhibit limited adaptability when market conditions change, while machine learning-based approaches frequently lack interpretability and generalization across assets. To solve these issues, this research explores an alternative approach in which large language models (LLMs) are incorporated into the alpha design and portfolio weighting process. Specifically, we introduce a novel framework that integrates a multi-agent LLM system with reinforcement learning to improve formulaic alpha generation and portfolio allocation. In our setup, DeepSeek serves as the generation agent to construct a diverse pool of formulaic alphas, while Gemini acts as the evaluation agent to filter and select the most promising candidates. The selected alphas are then incorporated into a Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) framework, which optimizes their portfolio weights to maximize risk-adjusted returns. Manually constructed alpha signals tend to exhibit limited adaptability when market conditions change, while machine learning-based approaches frequently lack interpretability and generalization across assets. To solve these issues, this research explores an alternative approach in which large language models (LLMs) are incorporated into the alpha design and portfolio weighting process. Specifically, we introduce a novel framework that integrates a multi-agent LLM system with reinforcement learning to improve formulaic alpha generation and portfolio allocation. In our setup, DeepSeek serves as the generation agent to construct a diverse pool of formulaic alphas, while Gemini acts as the evaluation agent to filter and select the most promising candidates. The selected alphas are then incorporated into a Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) framework, which optimizes their portfolio weights to maximize risk-adjusted returns. Empirical evaluations across seven major companies reveal that the multi-agent LLM + DDPG framework generally achieves higher cumulative returns than equal-weighted benchmarks and multi-agent PPO, though often with increased short-term risk. In contrast, single-agent PPO offers more stable, risk-controlled performance with smaller drawdowns. These results demonstrate that integrating LLM-generated signals with reinforcement learning can balance alpha exploitation and risk management, enabling adaptive and effective portfolio strategies across diverse market conditions.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6682038\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7096805\", \"title\": [\"Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Optimizing Care Pathways in Patients with Complex Chronic Conditions\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Complex chronic conditions (CCCs), comprising one of the main causes of morbidity and mortality, are often managed through predefined care pathways. These pathways advocate the application of therapeutic guidelines according to disease progression in order to enhance patient outcomes while minimizing costs. Considering patient heterogeneity, however, demands the establishment of tailored pathways. This work proposes a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework able to derive such pathways for representative patient groups characterized by a set of comorbidities, along with their clinical roles, who interact toward common objectives.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7096805\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "3374c9ca024bc8032650ea98b374759291be31a6213427f992c0cbcf5a50a18a", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "divergent_values", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.31390/gradschool_theses.6213", "doi:10.1016/j.ejcon.2025.101354", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.6682038", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.7096805"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.31390/gradschool_theses.6213", "https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejcon.2025.101354", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6682038", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7096805"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
